clue.text: Host is holding American tour, but it's one-sided

parts.note: a host is a crowd or throng, as is a mob

indicators.note: holding means the word is wraps round the next piece

parts.note: a tour is a trip

explanation.surface: A host carries an American round on a trip, though the arrangement favours one party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' signals a container. 'Host' looks like a party-giver but here means a crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: This famous loop of paper, given a half-twist, has only a single surface, a classic topological curiosity.

clue.text: Continually does a job after hours at a masterpiece of sound

parts.words: Continually does a job after hours
parts.note: to moonlight is to work a second job at night, and to moonlight on is to keep doing it
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone keeps working late shifts at a famous musical work.
explanation.walkthrough: Beethoven's Piano Sonata No. 14 is widely known by this name.
explanation.definitionFit: Beethoven's celebrated piano sonata is a masterpiece of music, i.e. of sound.

clue.text: Feast off a bone

indicators.note: off suggests gone bad or out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Dining on a bone that has gone bad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges A BONE. BEANO is informal British for a party or celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: A beano is British slang for a celebration or jolly meal, a feast.

clue.text: Relative article short on hygiene

parts.note: an uncle is a relative
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A family member writes a piece about lax hygiene.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unclean is dirty, lacking in cleanliness or hygiene.

clue.text: Surprise of persistent look officer kept up

indicators.note: kept means the look holds the officer inside

parts.note: a stare is a fixed, prolonged look

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the officer's letters are read upwards, backwards

parts.note: Lt is the abbreviation for lieutenant

explanation.surface: A lieutenant is startled by a long stare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Surprise of' reads like a noun phrase, but 'Surprise' is a verb here; 'up' and 'kept' work on the officer in a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To startle someone is to give them a sudden shock or surprise.

clue.text: Trust could be real nice

indicators.note: could be means the letters may form another word when rearranged

explanation.surface: Faith in someone might be very pleasant indeed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' rearranges REAL NICE.
explanation.definitionFit: Reliance is dependence on or confidence in someone, i.e. trust.

clue.text: Is it drawn for sickness or injury?

definitions.text: Is it drawn for sickness or injury?

parts.words: Is it drawn for sickness or injury?
parts.note: reads like a raffle for the ill, but means the way British NHS treatment depends on where you live, as if lots were drawn by address

explanation.surface: Wondering whether there is a prize draw for the sick and injured.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain, availability of NHS treatments has varied between areas, so whether you get care can seem a matter of chance by address code.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes unequal provision of health services between regions, like a draw decided by where you live.

clue.text: Melting icecap used as an emetic

indicators.note: melting suggests losing form and reshaping, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A polar icecap thaws and is turned into something to make you sick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Melting' rearranges ICECAP; 'used as' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Ipecac is a plant-derived medicine used to induce vomiting, so it is an emetic.

clue.text: Examples of indirect speech when about 11

indicators.note: about means the word for when goes round the team

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
a football or cricket side has eleven players

explanation.surface: Instances of indirect remarks made around eleven o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: '11' is not a time or a cross-reference to 11 across: a football or cricket team has eleven players.
explanation.definitionFit: Asides are remarks an actor makes to the audience, not directly to other characters, a form of indirect speech.

clue.text: US spies so put about by spin as lacking inspiration

parts.note: spin is public relations, PR

indicators.note: put about means turned round, so the spies and so are read backwards together

parts.note: the CIA is the American intelligence agency
taken as written

explanation.surface: American agents are given a spin-doctor's treatment that leaves them looking dull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put about' reverses the spies and 'so' together; 'by' just places spin alongside. Spin as PR is public relations.
explanation.definitionFit: Something prosaic is dull and matter-of-fact, without imagination or flair.

clue.text: Sailor crossing the ocean reflects on books that show it

indicators.note: reflects means the whole assembly is seen mirror-wise, back to front
crossing means the sailor goes across, inside the ocean's letters

parts.note: the ocean is the sea
an old salt is a seasoned sailor

explanation.surface: A mariner at sea muses over the reference books that chart the waters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reflects' turns the whole container backwards. 'it' in the definition points back to the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: Atlases are books of maps, and their pages depict the oceans along with the land.

clue.text: The most naïve permit incest

annotationWithheld.why: The most naive permit incest (9): the only parse reads 'incest' as 'in' (container indicator) plus CEST (fodder), one word doing two jobs, which the check refuses

clue.text: Bent like a Vatican media executive?

parts.note: the Vatican is the seat of the Roman Catholic church, RC
ED is short for editor, a newspaper executive

explanation.surface: Asking whether a Vatican newspaper editor is curved, a teasing riddle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'like' just links; A + RC (Roman Catholic) + ED (editor) spells the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Arced is a past participle meaning curved into an arc, so bent in shape.

clue.text: About time to lock up

parts.note: C stands for circa, Latin for about
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Approximately when someone will be imprisoned.
explanation.definitionFit: To cage someone is to confine them behind bars, the same as locking them up.

clue.text: Begs for others to plant crops, it's said

indicators.note: it's said means the phrase is heard rather than read, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: to inter is to bury or put in the ground; seeds are what crops grow from, standing in for them here

explanation.surface: Someone pleads on behalf of others for permission to sow fields.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it's said' signals that 'inter seeds' sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To intercede is to plead or mediate on behalf of someone else.

clue.text: Asian city that's mad about English mayor

indicators.note: about means the jumbled letters go round the mayor
mad suggests crazy disorder, so the letters of that's are rearranged

parts.note: Ken Livingstone was the first elected Mayor of London

explanation.surface: A city that has gone crazy over an English mayor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mad' rearranges the letters of that's to TASHT; Ken Livingstone was London's mayor when this puzzle appeared.
explanation.definitionFit: Tashkent is the capital of Uzbekistan in Central Asia.

clue.text: Former treatment for slipped discs: their removal

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
traction, stretching the spine with weights, was once used for slipped discs

explanation.surface: An old back therapy is contrasted with simply taking the damaged discs out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'their' ties the definition to the discs: the alternative to stretching them is taking them out.
explanation.definitionFit: Extraction is the act of pulling something out, a synonym for removal.

clue.text: Signal to raise hat to old mathematician

indicators.note: to raise in a down clue means the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: a cue is a signal to begin
lid is slang for hat

explanation.surface: A cue to tip one's hat to a mathematician of old.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'to raise' reads the signal from the bottom up, giving EUC.
explanation.definitionFit: Euclid was the ancient Greek mathematician known as the father of geometry.

clue.text: Breakfast equipment is sound, of course

indicators.note: is sound means the place name is spoken, its pronunciation giving the answer

parts.note: Towcester is a racecourse in Northamptonshire, England

explanation.surface: A breakfast gadget is in good working order, naturally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of course' looks like 'naturally' but points to a racecourse: TOWCESTER, an English racecourse, is pronounced the same as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A toaster is the kitchen appliance used for browning bread at breakfast.

clue.text: Her trouble rose with abandoned hope

indicators.note: abandoned suggests wild and unrestrained, so the letters are rearranged
rose in a down clue means the word goes up, read backwards

parts.note: to ail is to trouble

explanation.surface: A woman's grief grew as her hope was given up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoned' rearranges HOPE to OPHE; 'rose' reverses AIL to LIA. Hamlet's tragic heroine drowns, so the surface fits her.
explanation.definitionFit: Ophelia is a female character in Hamlet, so she is referred to as 'her'.

clue.text: Heavy going for pupil in school

indicators.note: in means the letter for pupil sits inside the school

parts.note: a school of whales or dolphins is also called a pod
L is a learner, as on a learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A student finds lessons a heavy slog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'school' means a group of whales, not a place of learning.
explanation.definitionFit: To plod is to walk with slow, heavy steps, which is heavy going.

clue.text: Unknown codes designed to entrap

indicators.note: designed means made into a new arrangement, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: in algebra y is an unknown quantity

explanation.surface: Secret ciphers are created to snare the unwary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'designed' rearranges Y + CODES; 'designed' also reads naturally with the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Decoys are lures used to tempt prey into a trap, so their purpose is entrapment.

clue.text: Companion absorbs a great deal of material

indicators.note: absorbs means the companion takes the next piece inside it

parts.note: CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British order
a lot means a great deal

explanation.surface: A friend soaks up a large quantity of fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: Companion of Honour is a British order of merit, abbreviated CH.
explanation.definitionFit: Cloth is woven fabric, i.e. material for clothes.

clue.text: Not believing the man is in Greek mode

indicators.note: in means the man and is go inside the Greek style

parts.note: Attic is the style or dialect of ancient Athens
he refers to a man

explanation.surface: A man raised in classical Greek ways is a sceptic.
explanation.walkthrough: Attic here is the adjective for ancient Athens and its Greek style, not a loft.
explanation.definitionFit: An atheistic person denies the existence of God, so is without religious belief.

clue.text: Old tape in use to maintain clear reproduction

indicators.note: in means the answer is found inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Vintage tape is kept in use to keep sound recordings clear.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across 'maintaIN CLEar'. INCLE is an old word for linen tape used for trimming.
explanation.definitionFit: Incle is an archaic term for a linen tape or braid used in trimming.

clue.text: Where cuckoo hatches is the ultimate in cuckoo

definitions.meaning: read as three words, ..., the place a cuckoo chick is hatched (in another bird's)
cuckoo means crazy or silly, so its ultimate is the silliest

explanation.surface: Musing that the cuckoo's birthplace is the height of madness.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as 'in a nest' for the first sense; cuckoos lay eggs in other birds' nests.
explanation.definitionFit: Inane means silly, so the superlative is the most foolish, the very peak of daftness.

clue.text: In general the church takes a line on unchaste behaviour

indicators.note: In means the church sits inside the general's name

parts.note: Robert E. Lee was the Confederate general
CH is the abbreviation for church
RY is the abbreviation for railway, a line

explanation.surface: Broadly, the church adopts a policy on immoral conduct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In general' looks like 'broadly' but splits: 'In' is the container signal; RY (railway) is the line.
explanation.definitionFit: Lechery is excessive lust, conduct that is the opposite of chaste.

clue.text: Train starts awfully late nearly every other time

indicators.note: awfully suggests something badly done, so the letters are jumbled
starts means only the first letter of train is used

explanation.surface: Train services are dreadfully behind schedule almost constantly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starts' gives T from Train; 'awfully' shuffles T + LATE + NEARLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Alternately means by turns, happening on every second occasion.
